idea-plugin.name: Implicit: Gaze-Triggered AI Assistance for Code Review
idea-plugin.description:
Gaze-triggered AI assistance for code review in IntelliJ IDEA and other JetBrains IDEs, inspired by the CodeGRITS research toolkit.

Open Tools → Implicit Gaze → Open Gaze Research… and follow Input → Scenario → Session → Start recording. Create a labelled session or reopen saved results. Setup stays paused until you start recording.
  • Mouse — mouse dwell as a proxy for gaze (no hardware needed).
  • Webcam eye tracker — estimated gaze from UnitEye's browser pipeline (webcam → MediaPipe → EyeMU), run in a hidden embedded browser, smoothed and corrected with a nine-target calibration and a five-target accuracy check. Fixed response presets stabilize code-line interaction; webcam precision still depends on the setup.
Gaze cursor — an optional blue gutter dot shows the accepted code-line target. Switch it on/off in Input or while recording; hidden by default.
Personalization — a guided target task selects a response preset and checks it on fresh targets. Save one IDE-user profile and reuse it across scenarios.
Gaze-assisted review — choose Explain, Compare or Review; context is prepared locally with quiet offers and a 30-second cooldown. Sending remains explicit in native AI Chat.
Gaze-driven review: stable block focus, reversible fading of viewed code, matching-identifier highlights, recent-view context for AI explanations, and a gaze-guided Review walkthrough: overview → files → code, with native AI Chat handoff, notes and user review marks. Tours use snapshots, not Git diffs. Replay Viewing Trace separately shows the recorded chronological route. Configure each feature under Settings → Tools → Implicit Gaze Features. Pause gaze effects to reveal all code.

AI context ready — a configurable dwell prepares a prompt locally. Click Ask JetBrains AI, review the context, copy it and open the installed JetBrains AI Chat. Paste and send there; choose AI Assistant or Junie Ask mode. Responses stay in native chat. GAZEAIDE does not choose a model or send HTTP AI requests.

Record and export gaze sessions: use the Experiment tab to start/stop recording. Stopped sessions save locally for reopening. Export CSV, JSON, or a self-contained HTML heatmap/replay page to see the estimated code-viewing path. Exposure does not establish understanding.

Optional remote study upload (experimental): configure an HTTPS research receiver or a Google Drive Apps Script receiver. Preview a reduced dataset, test with synthetic data, and upload manually or after future recordings. Off by default; excludes source code and paths. Requires separate testing and study-specific research, ethics and storage setup.

GAZEAIDE research tool. Started by Heidi Albarazi during her internship at JetBrains Research; subsequently updated by Ilia Zaharov (LinkedIn, Google Scholar). Estimated exposure does not establish comprehension or review correctness.
